format: Six transparent 2×2 sheets, four woman/newspaper poses per sheet

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset: HIGH DETAIL PHOTOGRAPHIC stop-motion poses of the single central woman and newspaper for a website hero. This is a replacement for a low-resolution sprite sheet: sharp facial features, natural skin texture, crisp sunglass edges, realistic fingers, and readable newspaper typography are the priority.
Image 1 is the exact identity, lighting, outfit and newspaper reference. If Image 2 is present it is only an adjacent animation sheet to match framing and continuity; always use Image 1 for facial detail.
Create exactly FOUR frames in a precise 2-column by 2-row grid, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. NOT more than four figures. Tall portrait canvas, aim for 2048 x 2560 or highest available resolution. Each quadrant is one full portrait cutout with the top of hair, both hands, the complete newspaper, and hips visible. Same camera, identical subject scale and center and waist baseline in every frame. Fill each cell generously: head at about 4% of cell height, waist at 97%; leave 4% clear horizontal margins even when the paper is fully opened. No overlapping quadrants or cropped paper edges. Fixed studio viewpoint, no camera motion.
Genuine transparent alpha background, clean cutout edges, no scene or backdrop, no shadows outside the figure, no labels, no gridlines. Do not add the camera, other hands, headphones, light effects, logos or extra props. Only this SAME adult woman, coral cat-eye sunglasses, slick dark hair, gold hoops, black outfit, and cream broadsheet newspaper.
Typography: retain the exact original newspaper design consistently from frame to frame. Black serif masthead "THE SONAR REPORT"; reversed line "YOUR MARKET, ON CAMERA"; three lines "The competitors in your niche", "The creators posting for them", "The clips that broke out"; italic "Every number cited. Every video linked."; boxed footer "HEAR WHAT YOUR MARKET IS SAYING". Folded sections may naturally hide text but NEVER reflow or rewrite the printed layout between poses. The paper always has the same size and center crease.
Motion must be small, consecutive, anatomically plausible stop-motion increments. Preserve facial identity and proportions, skin tone, eyewear, paper texture and typography. No blurry face, smooth plastic skin, enlarged head, cartoon look, interpolation ghosts, or warping letters.

SHEET 1, animation frames 01–04, OPENING. In each frame she is reading with her chin lowered slightly, calm expression. At start the broadsheet is folded along its vertical middle so the two hands are closer together. Frame 01: newspaper 40% opened. Frame 02: 45% opened, right hand (viewer left) moves out a little. Frame 03: 50% opened. Frame 04: 55% opened, chin lifts very slightly. These are four clearly distinct small stages of physically unfolding the SAME newspaper, NOT four different newspapers.

SHEET 2, animation frames 05–08, FINISH OPENING. Continue the small unfolding movement from the supplied previous sheet. Frame 05: paper 65% opened, chin still slightly down. Frame 06: paper 78% opened, chin begins lifting. Frame 07: paper 90% opened, looking up. Frame 08: paper 100% opened matching the original reference's wide broadsheet, looking forward, calm expression. Hands spread naturally with the paper. Keep subject scale and waist baseline identical across all four frames.

SHEET 3, animation frames 09–12, NOTICE THE CAMERA. The newspaper remains FULLY OPEN at the reference position and does not change size, print or shape. Frame 11: head turns 6 degrees toward viewer LEFT, chin up slightly. Frame 12: head turns 9 degrees toward viewer LEFT, lips softly part in anticipation. Tiny continuous movement; no camera or flash drawn.

SHEET 4, animation frames 13–16, CAMERA REACTION. Newspaper remains fully open, same printed typography and fixed size. Frame 13: the instant of a camera flash from viewer LEFT: surprised but subtle, eyebrows lift above sunglasses, lips slightly parted, head recoils backwards a little and shoulders lift 1 cm. Do not draw actual light. Frame 14: shoulders settle halfway and a hint of a smile appears, still looking to viewer LEFT. Frame 15: gentle confident closed-mouth smile, head turns halfway back toward front. Frame 16: warm restrained closed-mouth smile toward front, shoulders relaxed. Do not exaggerate or open mouth widely; continuous small changes.

SHEET 6, animation frames 21–24, CLOSE THE LOOP. Continue from the previous listening pose, preserve same camera and framing. Frame 21: looking slightly down at the fully opened paper, neutral expression. Frame 22: fold the newspaper inward along its vertical center crease to 80% open, hands move toward center. Frame 23: paper 60% open, eyes down. Frame 24: newspaper 40% open and the exact reading pose of the initial opening frame, chin lowered and neutral expression. The printed text must stay fixed to the paper and simply disappear into folds, never reflow.
Reference image 3 is the first four frames. The final folded paper, chin angle, crop and neutral expression must closely match its FIRST (top-left) frame, so the loop joins cleanly.
